newsitem.title: JAPAN: DDI to buy capacity in KDD undersea cable.
newsitem.headline: DDI to buy capacity in KDD undersea cable.

text.p: Domestic long-distance telecommunications operator DDI Corp said on Friday it would buy 20 percent of the data transmission capacity in undersea fiber-optic cables that international telecoms operator Kokusai Denshin Denwa Co Ltd (KDD) plans to lay around Japan.

"We have basically agreed on the purchase," a DDI spokesman told Reuters, adding that they still have to discuss details, including the cost. "We will negotiate over specifics and would like to sign the agreement in early 1997," he said.
DDI is 21.7 percent owned by Kyocera Corp.
The new cable, in which DDI will have a 20 percent share, will have a data transmission capacity of 100 gigabits per second, the DDI spokesman said.
Economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun said on Friday that KDD will start laying the cables in the second half of 1997, with operations starting in 1999.
DDI will pay KDD 40 billion to 50 billion yen, the newspaper said.
DDI wants to boost capacity to meet increasing demand for telecommunications services, such as the Internet and image transmission, the paper said.
